question: Consider the function $f(n)$ defined for all positive integers as follows: $f(n)=\begin{cases}n+1,&\text{if }n\text{ is odd},\\ n/2,&\text{if }n\text{ is even}.\end{cases}$ Let $f^{(k)}$ denote $f$ applied $k$ times; e.g., $f^{(1)}(n)=f(n)$, $f^{(2)}(n)=f(f(n))$ and so on. Then

options.A: there exists one integer $k_0$ such that for all $n\ge2$, $f^{(k_0)}(n)=1$
options.B: for each $n\ge2$, there exists an integer $k$ (depending on $n$) such that $f^{(k)}(n)=1$
options.C: for each $n\ge2$, there exists an integer $k$ (depending on $n$) such that $f^{(k)}(n)$ is a multiple of 4
options.D: for each $n$, $f^{(k)}(n)$ is a decreasing function of $k$

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level
